nodes.text: ASSESS FOR DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS: Has the child had any difficulties with age-appropriate milestones across all developmental areas (or difficulties with school, communicating, interacting, and self-care for older children/adolescents)?
Are there signs/symptoms suggesting nutritional deficiency (including iodine), anaemia, malnutrition, or acute/chronic infectious illness (including ear infection and HIV/AIDS)?
Manage conditions using Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) or other available guidelines.
Assess the child for visual and/or hearing impairment. Does the child fail visual assessments (fails to look at eyes, follow object) or hearing assessments (fails to react to loud noise, turn head)?
Consult with a specialist for visual and/or hearing evaluation.
Developmental Delay/Disorder

Protocol 1 (Developmental Delay/Disorder): Provide guidance on child well-being, psychoeducation, and parenting advice. Provide carer support, liaise with teachers, and link with Community-Based Rehabilitation. Offer Parent Skills Training. Refer to specialist for further assessment. DO NOT offer pharmacological treatment. Follow-up: Reassess every 3 months or more; if no improvement, further deterioration, or danger, refer to specialist.
ASSESS FOR PROBLEMS WITH INATTENTION OR HYPERACTIVITY: Is the child/adolescent overactive, unable to stay still for long, easily distracted, or moving restlessly?
Are symptoms persistent, severe, and inappropriate for the developmental level? (Present in multiple settings, lasted at least 6 months, and causing considerable difficulty with daily functioning?)
Problems with Behaviour

Protocol 2 (Problems with Behaviour): Provide guidance on child well-being and improving behaviour. Assess for and manage stressors. Liaise with teachers and link with community resources. Follow-up: Offer regular follow-up to reassess symptoms.
Rule out physical conditions that can resemble ADHD. Does the child/adolescent have thyroid diseases, infectious illness, or uncontrolled pain?
Treat the physical condition.
Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)

Protocol 3 (ADHD): Provide psychoeducation, guidance on improving behaviour, and carer support. Manage stressors, liaise with teachers, and consider behavioural interventions. If interventions fail and child is >=6 years, refer to specialist for methylphenidate. Follow-up: Every 3 months. If no improvement after 6 months of psychosocial treatment, consult specialist for methylphenidate. Monitor height, weight, BP if on medication.

ASSESS FOR CONDUCT DISORDER: Does the child/adolescent show repeated aggressive, disobedient, or defiant behaviour (e.g., arguing, extreme irritability, tantrums, fighting, bullying, destructiveness, stealing)?
Are symptoms persistent, severe, inappropriate for developmental level, present in different settings for at least 6 months, and causing considerable difficulty?
Conduct Disorder

Protocol 4 (Conduct Disorder): Provide psychoeducation and guidance on improving behaviour. Manage stressors, provide carer support, and liaise with teachers. DO NOT offer pharmacological treatment. Follow-up: Every 3 months. If no improvement or danger to adolescent, refer to specialist.

ASSESS FOR EMOTIONAL DISORDERS: Is the child/adolescent often feeling irritable/down, lost interest, having many worries/fears, frequently complaining of physical sickness, or avoiding certain situations?
Is there considerable difficulty with daily functioning in personal, family, social, educational, occupational or other areas?
Problems with Emotions

Protocol 5 (Problems with Emotions): Provide guidance on child well-being, psychoeducation, and parenting advice. Assess for and manage stressors. Liaise with teachers and link with available community resources.

Rule out physical conditions that can resemble or exacerbate emotional disorders. Are there any signs/symptoms of thyroid diseases, infectious illness, anaemia, obesity, malnutrition, asthma, or medication side-effects?
Manage the physical condition.
Is the person an adolescent who has problems with mood (feeling irritable, down or sad) OR has lost interest in or enjoyment of activities?
Emotional Disorder

Protocol 6 (Emotional Disorder): Provide psychoeducation, guidance on well-being, and carer support. Assess/manage stressors. Consider behavioural intervention or interpersonal therapy. DO NOT prescribe pharmacological treatment as first line or for children <12 years. Follow-up: Once a month. Refer to specialist if no improvement after 6 months of psychosocial treatment.

Has the adolescent had several additional symptoms (e.g., disturbed sleep, appetite/weight change, worthlessness/guilt, fatigue, reduced concentration, indecisiveness, agitation, hopelessness, suicidal thoughts) most days for the last 2 weeks?
Is there considerable difficulty with daily functioning in personal, family, social, educational, occupational or other areas due to these depressive symptoms?
Depression (Adolescent)

Protocol 6 (Depression): Rule out manic episode or normal reaction to major loss. Provide psychoeducation, guidance on well-being, and carer support. Consider interpersonal therapy. Follow-up: Once a month. If psychological interventions are ineffective after 6 months and adolescent is >=12 years old, consult specialist for Fluoxetine (no other SSRIs or TCAs). Monitor weekly for first month if prescribed.
Is there an imminent risk of suicide or suicidal thoughts?
Assess and manage suicide risk immediately.
ASSESS FOR OTHER PRIORITY MNS CONDITIONS: Are there any other concurrent MNS conditions (e.g., disorders due to substance use, or epilepsy for children with developmental delay)?
Assess and manage concurrent MNS conditions (incorporating appropriate specific condition management for substance use or epilepsy).

ASSESS THE HOME ENVIRONMENT: Are the emotional, behavioural or developmental problems a reaction to or aggravated by a distressing or frightening situation (e.g., maltreatment, exposure to violence, severe stressors)?
Refer to child protection services if necessary. Explore and manage stressors. Ensure child/adolescent's safety. Arrange additional support and consider psychosocial interventions.
Do the carers have any priority MNS condition that could impact their ability to care for the child/adolescent (especially depression and disorders due to substance use)?
Assess and manage for carer MNS conditions. Offer support for their personal, social, and mental health needs (Carer Support).
Is the child getting adequate opportunities for play and social interaction/communication at home?
Provide advice on age-appropriate stimulation and parenting. Consider need for additional support including referral to child protection services.
ASSESS THE SCHOOL ENVIRONMENT: Is the child/adolescent in school?
Provide information regarding educational services and educate carer on importance of keeping the child/adolescent in school as much as possible.
Is the child/adolescent being bullied, picked on, not able to participate and learn, or refusing to attend school?
Liaise with teachers and other school staff. Explore reasons for absence and try to help the child/adolescent return to school as soon as possible.
End of Assessment and Management for Child & Adolescent Mental & Behavioural Disorders.
